items.note: bound(42) passes an arbitrary number to show that a number is rejected by the types. The value has no unit and no reason to name.
app.listen(3000) uses a bare port number. A named port constant is what the rule asks for.
42 stands for any value that is not a function in a test of the argument check. A name would add nothing.
buf[0] === 0x5b compares with the byte of an opening bracket. The reader must know the character code.
buf[0] !== 0x20 compares with the byte of a space. The reader must know the character code.
parameterLimit: 10.1 is named by its property key, and the test title says it is a floating point limit.
Buffer.alloc(999, ...) is a test body size. The expected ETag two lines below depends on it, so a name could help, but the size itself is arbitrary.

The if on line 679 is at a third level, and its body is only a throw. The rule text says such a guard clause does not add a level. The engine exempts a guard only directly under a function or a loop, not under another if.
q[0][3] reads the reject callback by its position in a four-item tuple. The index 3 has no name.
The if on line 132 is inside a try, inside a while loop, and its body is only return t. By the rule text a guard clause does not add a level; the engine counts this one because its parent is a try.
Same shape as tslib.es6.js:132: an if with only a return, inside a try, inside a while loop.
The if (d = decorators[i]) is inside the for loop, which is the else branch of the if on line 106. That is a third level and the limit is two.
